title: Macalinao v. Bank of the Philippine Islands
summary: The Supreme Court struck down the 3% monthly interest rate and other charges imposed by BPI on credit card balances as unconscionable. The Court reduced the interest to 1% per month and the penalty charge to 1% per month.
doctrine: Credit card interest rates are not exempt from judicial review. While the Usury Law ceiling has been lifted, courts may still reduce unconscionable interest rates on credit cards. A 3% monthly interest (36% per annum) on credit card balances is excessive and may be equitably reduced.
fullText:
PERALTA, J.:

The issue is whether the interest rate and penalty charges imposed by BPI on the credit card balance of the petitioner are valid and enforceable.

While the Usury Law has been effectively suspended, the Court has consistently held that interest rates imposed on obligations may be reduced when they are unconscionable. The 3% monthly interest rate (or 36% per annum) imposed by BPI is iniquitous and unconscionable.

The Court equitably reduces the monthly interest rate to 1% and the monthly penalty charge to 1%. Credit card agreements, being contracts of adhesion, are construed strictly against the party who drafted them.
